title: Traffic Collision Report
subtitle: Non-injury collision - private property

sections.heading: Incident
fields: Harbor Point Shopping Center parking lot, 2200 block of Harbor Ave, Maple Harbor, OR
Backing - vehicle backing from parking stall
Proceeding eastbound in parking aisle, approx. 5 mph
Rear bumper cover pushed in and cracked at right corner; right rear quarter panel creased and scraped with gray paint transfer; right tail lamp lens broken
Backing northbound out of parking stall on south side of aisle
Scrapes and blue paint transfer on left corner of rear bumper

diagram.caption: Scene diagram - not to scale. Unit 1 eastbound in aisle; Unit 2 backing north from stall. X marks area of impact.

statements: Stated they were driving slowly through the lot looking for a parking space when the pickup backed out of a stall on their right and struck the rear right corner of their vehicle.
Stated they were backing out of the parking stall, checked their mirrors and did not see Unit 1 until they felt the impact.
narrative: On 11/12/2026 at approximately 1431 hrs I was dispatched to a reported non-injury collision in the Harbor Point Shopping Center parking lot, 2200 block of Harbor Ave. I arrived at 1446 hrs and contacted both drivers, who were standing near their vehicles. Neither driver reported any injury.

Unit 1 was stopped in the east-west parking aisle facing east. Unit 2 was stopped partially out of a parking stall on the south side of the aisle, with its rear toward the aisle. Statements from both drivers indicate that Unit 2 was backing north out of the stall as Unit 1 passed eastbound, and the rear of Unit 2 struck the right rear corner of Unit 1.

I observed fresh damage to the right rear of Unit 1. The rear bumper cover was pushed in and cracked at the right corner, the right rear quarter panel behind the rear wheel was creased and scraped with gray paint transfer, and the right tail lamp lens was broken. Pieces of red lamp lens were on the pavement next to Unit 1. I observed scrapes and blue paint transfer on the left corner of the rear bumper of Unit 2. The paint transfer on each vehicle was consistent in color with the other vehicle.

No independent witnesses were identified. Both vehicles were drivable and were driven from the scene. The collision occurred on private property and no citations were issued. Both drivers exchanged information in my presence and were provided with this report number.
